text: Yellowstone just erupted. Here's what's going to happen.
First, a wave of burning hot ash and gas races down the mountains at over fifty miles an hour.
The ash cloud is so big it makes its own wind, and pushes ash over nine hundred miles against the wind.
Ash falls across the country like gray snow. Near the volcano, it piles up more than three feet deep.
Get rain on it, and the ash gets twice as heavy. Roofs start caving in.
And don't breathe it in. Ash is tiny, sharp bits of rock and glass.
Planes stop flying, because ash melts inside jet engines.
Then the whole planet can get several degrees colder, for years.
The good news? The chance of this happening in any year is about one in seven hundred thirty thousand.
And that's what happens when Yellowstone erupts.
